findings.issue_text: Remote RSS/embed content is stored with cook_method = :raw_html and rendered via `raw post.cooked` without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from feed content containing `<script>` or `onerror=` handlers (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8-40, app/models/post.rb:130, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19)
PollFeed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` through with no tag whitelist at all, unlike import_remote which uses a Readability whitelist (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34)

embed.js origin validation uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring test on attacker-controlled `e.origin`, so any origin that is a substring of the configured URL passes; should compare parsed origins with `===` (app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:15)

`parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` interpolates the raw referer header into a JS string literal; only the host is validated, so path/query are attacker-controlled and injected into script context (app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:11)
`<%- end if %>` is invalid Ruby and causes a SyntaxError when the template is compiled (app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6)

`post.present?` is true even for an unsaved record with validation errors, so `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: nil, topic_id: nil)` runs and raises inside the transaction; should check `post.persisted?` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22-28)
`setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies between calls the key never expires and the embed URL is throttled forever (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-31)

Check-then-insert on `embed_url` races between concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs, causing ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique after a duplicate topic and post have already been created and leaked (app/models/topic_embed.rb:16-30)

`i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError on feed items lacking `<content:encoded>`, and with `sidekiq_options retry: false` one such item aborts the entire poll and silently drops remaining items (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34)

`Kernel#open(url)` executes a subprocess for strings starting with `|` and follows arbitrary redirects, enabling command injection and SSRF to internal addresses (app/models/topic_embed.rb:44, app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:32)

Adding `force: true` to an already-released migration drops the existing `top_topics` table and its data if re-run, with no benefit to anyone who already migrated (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4)

`perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, running a full feed fetch, parse, and import synchronously on every cache-miss embed request with no timeout (lib/topic_retriever.rb:44-46)

Spec stubs `TopicRetriever.new`/`retrieve` but the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so the mock expectation doesn't match the controller's actual collaborator (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-49)

`TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil while best.html.erb immediately calls `@topic_view.posts`, so the test asserts success on a template that would raise (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:52-54)

No test that a referer from a different host is rejected, so the negative access-control branch of `ensure_embeddable` and the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue are never exercised (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb)
`absolutize_urls` only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with `/`, leaving document-relative (`images/x.jpg`) and protocol-relative (`//cdn/x.jpg`) URLs broken (app/models/topic_embed.rb:52-67)
`contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place and raises on frozen strings (app/models/topic_embed.rb:12)

SHA1 is computed over the locale-translated footer, so changing site locale marks every previously imported topic as changed and triggers a spurious revision of every post (app/models/topic_embed.rb:12)

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remote RSS/embed content is stored with cook_method = :raw_html and rendered via `raw post.cooked` without sanitization, allowing stored XSS from feed content containing `<script>` or `onerror=` handlers (app/models/topic_embed.rb:8-40, app/models/post.rb:130, app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to return `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using content sourced from RSS (`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`) and does not sanitize/strip dangerous tags or attributes; `absolutize_urls` rewrites links/images but preserves arbitrary HTML. The embed view then renders this HTML using `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (and `post.cooked == post.raw` for raw_html), which will execute any `<script>` or event-handler payloads stored in the imported content, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed passes `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` through with no tag whitelist at all, unlike import_remote which uses a Readability whitelist (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:34)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the feed item body is taken as `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` and passed into `TopicEmbed.import(...)` with no sanitization/whitelisting. `TopicEmbed.import` creates the post via `PostCreator` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. By contrast, `import_remote` uses `ruby-readability` with explicit `tags`/`attributes` allowlists before importing. So the diff introduces a verifiable security/correctness problem: arbitrary HTML from an external RSS/ATOM feed can be stored and rendered as raw HTML (XSS risk).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `post.present?` is true even for an unsaved record with validation errors, so `TopicEmbed.create!(post_id: nil, topic_id: nil)` runs and raises inside the transaction; should check `post.persisted?` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22-28)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code checks `if post.present?` after `post = creator.create` and then uses `post.topic_id`/`post.id` in `TopicEmbed.create!`. The proposed issue hinges on `PostCreator#create` returning a non-nil `Post` object that is *not persisted* (and thus has nil ids) when creation fails. That behavior is not shown in this diff, and the diff does not demonstrate that `creator.create` can return an unsaved-but-present record here (especially since it is called with `skip_validations: true`). Without knowing `PostCreator#create`’s return contract from code in the diff, it’s not a verifiable defect introduced by this change; it’s a hypothetical about external behavior. Even if `create!` raised, it would rollback the transaction, which may be acceptable failure handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic; if the process dies between calls the key never expires and the embed URL is throttled forever (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-31)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the throttle key is created with `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then TTL is applied in a separate call `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. These two operations are not atomic; if the process/thread crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will remain without an expiration, causing `setnx` to fail forever for that embed_url and effectively throttling retrieval permanently until the key is manually deleted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Check-then-insert on `embed_url` races between concurrent RetrieveTopic jobs, causing ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique after a duplicate topic and post have already been created and leaked (app/models/topic_embed.rb:16-30)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does a non-atomic “check then insert”: it queries `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and, if blank, proceeds to create a post/topic and then `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` while a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` is added in the migration. Under concurrent calls for the same `embed_url`, both can observe `embed.blank?` and then one will hit the unique constraint, raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (no rescue/handling here), causing the job/request to fail. The finding’s “leaked duplicate topic and post” part is less certain because the post/embed creation is wrapped in `Topic.transaction`, which would typically roll back on the exception, but the race/RecordNotUnique risk itself is real and verifiable from the diff.

The candidate adds extra context about Sidekiq retry behavior and job aborting, but the underlying issue matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding `force: true` to an already-released migration drops the existing `top_topics` table and its data if re-run, with no benefit to anyone who already migrated (db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:4)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. Since this is an already-dated migration, if it is ever re-run against a database where `top_topics` already exists (e.g., manual `db:migrate:up VERSION=...`, a partially-migrated DB, or other nonstandard rerun scenarios), it can silently drop existing data instead of raising an error, with no benefit for databases that have already successfully applied the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline, running a full feed fetch, parse, and import synchronously on every cache-miss embed request with no timeout (lib/topic_retriever.rb:44-46)

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, perform_retrieve does call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, before falling back to `fetch_http`. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` performs `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`, which is a synchronous network fetch/parse/import and does not specify any timeouts in the code shown. This work can therefore run synchronously as part of an embed-miss retrieval (though it runs inside the background retrieval flow, not directly in the controller request).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec stubs `TopicRetriever.new`/`retrieve` but the controller enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so the mock expectation doesn't match the controller's actual collaborator (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:44-49)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `EmbedController#best` enqueues a background job when no embed is found: `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: embed_url)` and does not call `TopicRetriever` directly. However, `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` (the “tells the topic retriever to work…” example) sets expectations on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retriever.retrieve`. Since the controller’s actual collaborator is `Jobs.enqueue` (and the job later uses `TopicRetriever`), the spec’s mock expectations don’t match the code path and would fail/are testing the wrong behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `TopicView.expects(:new)` returns nil while best.html.erb immediately calls `@topic_view.posts`, so the test asserts success on a template that would raise (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:52-54)

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `topic_id` is present it assigns `@topic_view = TopicView.new(...)` and then renders the `best` template. In the controller spec, `TopicView.expects(:new).with(...)` (Mocha) will indeed return `nil` unless `.returns(...)` is specified, so `@topic_view` would be `nil` *if the ERB were actually executed*. However, RSpec controller specs do **not** render views by default (unless `render_views` is enabled), so `best.html.erb` is not evaluated and no `@topic_view.posts` call occurs. Also, in the real app `TopicView.new` returns a proper object, so the template would not raise. This makes the finding a misreading/overstatement rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that a referer from a different host is rejected, so the negative access-control branch of `ensure_embeddable` and the `URI::InvalidURIError` rescue are never exercised (spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb)

adjudication.rationale: In the added controller, `ensure_embeddable` rejects requests when `URI(request.referer).host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and also rescues `URI::InvalidURIError` to raise invalid access. The new `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` covers: missing `embed_url`, missing `embeddable_host`, and missing referer, plus the success case with a same-host referer. It does not include a test where `request.referer` is present but from a different host, nor a test with an invalid referer URI, so those negative branches (host mismatch and the rescue) are indeed unexercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `absolutize_urls` only rewrites hrefs/srcs starting with `/`, leaving document-relative (`images/x.jpg`) and protocol-relative (`//cdn/x.jpg`) URLs broken (app/models/topic_embed.rb:52-67)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the code only rewrites `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')`. Any document-relative URLs like `images/x.jpg` or `../img.png` are left untouched, which will resolve relative to the Discourse site when rendered and thus be incorrect for imported content. The finding is therefore verifiably true regarding document-relative URLs (though protocol-relative `//cdn/x.jpg` URLs are already absolute and not necessarily “broken”).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` mutates the caller's string in place and raises on frozen strings (app/models/topic_embed.rb:12)

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends to the String passed in by the caller, which is an in-place mutation of the argument. This is directly verifiable from the diff and can cause unexpected side effects if the caller reuses `contents` after calling `import`. Also, if a caller ever passes a frozen string, `<<` will raise (FrozenError in newer Rubies), since `<<` requires the receiver to be mutable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SHA1 is computed over the locale-translated footer, so changing site locale marks every previously imported topic as changed and triggers a spurious revision of every post (app/models/topic_embed.rb:12)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends a locale-dependent footer via `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', ...)` to `contents` and then computes `content_sha1 = Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(contents)`. Because the SHA1 is stored in `topic_embeds.content_sha1` and later used to decide whether to revise an existing post (`if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1 ... revisor.revise! ...`), changing the server/site locale (which changes the translation string) will change the computed SHA1 even when the underlying article content is unchanged. On the next re-import/poll, this will trigger unnecessary revisions for all previously imported items.
